questions.stem: A 43-year-old woman presented with a 9-month history of arthralgia and swelling of wrists and small joints of her hands bilaterally. Her symptoms had not resolved despite regular use of nonsteroidal antiinflammatories. She was otherwise fit and well and worked as a systems analyst for a large multinational company. She associated the start of her symptoms with a business trip to Brazil during which time she had a brief febrile illness with myalgia, a mild rash, and skin peeling from the palms of her hands.
questions.lead_in: What is the most likely infective cause?
questions.explanation: Chikungunya virus Parvovirus B19, chikungunya, and rubella are all associated with arthritis, most commonly of the small joints such as hands and wrists. The arthritis associated with rubella usually lasts up to a few weeks. Chronic arthritis is rare in rubella but is described in both parvovirus and notably chikungunya, in which reportedly up to 35% of cases may develop chronic joint symptoms. Chikungunya was found for the first time in the Americas as recently as 2013 but has since been responsible for hundreds of thousands of cases in North, Central, and South America.

questions.model_answer: a) Family Togaviridae (genus Alphavirus). b) Aedes aegypti (or Aedes albopictus). c) (1) Sub-Saharan/East Africa (2) India and Southeast Asia and the Indian Ocean islands (Reunion) [also the Caribbean/Americas]. d) Adults: (1) severe polyarticular arthralgia/arthritis favouring the small joints (2) maculopapular, often pruritic rash (face/neck then trunk, limbs, palms, soles); Children: CNS involvement (seizures/convulsions). e) Mild leukopenia with relative lymphocytosis (markedly elevated ESR, positive CRP).
questions.beyond_mandell: Family Togaviridae is standard classification; the chapter text names only the alphavirus genus.
questions.cohort_conflict: Cohort lists thrombocytopenia/lymphopenia as the typical hematological finding; Mandell describes mild leukopenia with relative lymphocytosis in ordinary CHIK fever (thrombocytopenia/lymphopenia are features of neonatal mother-to-child disease).

cohort_answer.text: Family: Togaviridae (genus: Alphavirus). Vectors: Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus (also transmit dengue). Endemic regions: West Africa, Asia, Caribbean. Clinical features - Adults: Severe symmetric polyarthralgia of small joints (>10 joints, hands/wrists/ankles); Rash (usually ≥3d after onset, maculopapular, may be pruritic, trunk/limbs/face/palms/soles). Children: Neurologic involvement (seizures/encephalopathy); GI haemorrhage; Bullous skin lesions. Hematological finding: Thrombocytopenia, lymphopenia.

cohort_answer.text: a) Togaviridae (not Flaviviridae), Genus: Alphavirus (others: Eastern/Western Equine viruses, Ross River virus, Venezuela Equine). b) Symptoms in adults: Maculopapular rash, Arthralgia, Conjunctivitis, Headache. Unique to peds: atypical dermatologic manifestations (symmetric vesiculobullous skin lesions, acrocyanosis, lower limb edema); more likely to cause neurologic disease (encephalitis). c) Southeast Asia; West Africa; South America (now extended to Caribbean); Pacific Islands. d) Leukopenia and thrombocytopenia, but not as commonly seen as in Dengue.

cohort_answer.text: Family: Togaviridae. Adults: arthralgia/arthritis, rash (maculopapular), fever, fatigue. Kids (neonatal): more likely neurologic disease (meningoencephalitis) or seizures, acrocyanosis without hemodynamic instability, symmetrical vesiculobullous lesions, edema of lower extremities. Lab abnormality: lymphopenia and thrombocytopenia (also hepatic transaminitis). Vector: Aedes aegypti, Aedes albopictus.

cohort_answer.text: A) Togaviridae. B) Africa, Indian Ocean islands, Mediterranean, South Asia, SE Asia, East Asia, Pacific Islands, Caribbean/South America. C) Rash (flush over face/neck, macular, may be pruritic, spreads centrifugally); polyarthritis (polyarticular, small joints and sites of prior injury, rarely effusions); tenosynovitis. D) CNS symptoms including seizures. E) Leukopenia with lymphocyte predominance; elevated CRP and ESR; transaminase elevation (inconsistent); thrombocytopenia rare.
